verdict.rationale: Supabase Auth documents that, after OAuth sign-in, it returns the provider token and provider refresh token. An app can use these to call the third-party provider's API under the user's consented authority, which is a thin, direct form of delegated third-party access. Nothing shows a managed token vault, token exchange, agent-oriented token issuance, or server-side storage and refresh of those provider tokens. missing for 10: token vault storing and refreshing third-party tokens on the user's behalf, token exchange flow, agent/tool-call-specific delegation, scoped short-lived issuance for arbitrary third-party APIs, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent obtain short-lived, user-consented tokens for third-party APIs (token vault/exchange) so tool calls run under the user's delegated authority

citations.quote: You can use the provider token and provider refresh token returned to make API calls to the OAuth provider.
